correctness.rationale: PASS: For q≥3, one systematic check position attached to q constant messages produces nonconstant pairs (a,t_a) oriented up or down. Three or more messages force two equal signs and hence a positive-affine collision; thus r_sys≥2. Two reserved reference symbols (0,1) attain equality. For unrestricted q≥3,k≥2, primitive nonconstant triples with minimum zero number 3 F(q−1)+3, with F(m)=#{1≤a,b≤m:gcd(a,b)=1}>m²/2, giving at least q² nonequivalent triples. Appending arbitrary k−2 payload symbols preserves nonconfusability, proving one-symbol overhead. For k=1 there are only two length-two positive-affine orientation classes; q≥3 requires two checks. Binary one-check construction covers every k. Finite independent gcd/normalized-affine tests corroborate q=2..13 but are not the universal argument.
